{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Release Binary

on:
  push:
    tags:
      # 只认版本 tag，避免非版本 tag（如 test-xxx）被当成版本号发布出去。
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "Run snapshot build without publishing"
        type: boolean
        default: true
        required: false
      ref:
        description: "Git ref to test (branch or commit SHA)"
        type: string
        default: ""
        required: false
      afrogweb_ref:
        description: "afrogweb Git ref to build (branch, tag, or commit SHA)"
        type: string
        default: "main"
        required: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      GOPROXY: https://proxy.golang.org,direct
      GOSUMDB: sum.golang.org
      AFROGWEB_REF: ${{ github.event.inputs.afrogweb_ref || 'main' }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.ref }}

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v4
        with:
          go-version: 1.24.1
          cache: true

      # afrogweb 用 pnpm 管理依赖（仓库提交了 pnpm-lock.yaml）。版本与其 lockfile
      # 保持一致，避免不同 pnpm 主版本读同一个 lockfile 时行为漂移。
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10.32.0
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Go modules download
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          go mod download

      - name: Build and copy afrogweb assets
        env:
          AFROGWEB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AFROGWEB_TOKEN }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          WEB_ASSETS_READY=false

          AFROGWEB_REPO_URL="https://github.com/zan8in/afrogweb.git"
          if [ -n "${AFROGWEB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            AFROGWEB_REPO_URL="https://x-access-token:${AFROGWEB_TOKEN}@github.com/zan8in/afrogweb.git"
          fi

          REF_PRIMARY="${AFROGWEB_REF}"
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "push" ] && [ -n "${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}" ]; then
            REF_PRIMARY="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          fi
          REF_FALLBACK="${AFROGWEB_REF}"

          try_clone() {
            local ref="$1"
            rm -rf _afrogweb_tmp
            git clone --depth 1 --branch "${ref}" "${AFROGWEB_REPO_URL}" _afrogweb_tmp
          }

          clone_with_log() {
            local ref="$1"
            local out
            out="$(try_clone "${ref}" 2>&1)" && return 0
            out="$(echo "${out}" | sed -E 's#https://x-access-token:[^@]+@github.com#https://x-access-token:***@github.com#g')"
            echo "[afrogweb] clone failed for ref=${ref}" >&2
            echo "${out}" | tail -n 80 >&2
            return 1
          }

          if clone_with_log "${REF_PRIMARY}"; then
            echo "AFROGWEB_REF_EFFECTIVE=${REF_PRIMARY}"
          elif [ "${REF_PRIMARY}" != "${REF_FALLBACK}" ] && clone_with_log "${REF_FALLBACK}"; then
            echo "AFROGWEB_REF_EFFECTIVE=${REF_FALLBACK}"
          else
            rm -rf _afrogweb_tmp || true
          fi

          if [ -d "_afrogweb_tmp" ]; then
            cd _afrogweb_tmp
            node -v
            pnpm -v || true
            npm -v
            git rev-parse HEAD
            if [ -d "static/docs" ] && [ -d "../docs" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A static/docs 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
              cp -R ../docs/* static/docs/ || true
            fi
            # afrogweb 的依赖以 pnpm-lock.yaml 为准。走 npm 是无 lockfile 的浮动安装，
            # 且在 npm 10 的 peer 解析里会抛 "Cannot read properties of null (reading
            # 'edgesOut')" 而中断发布；lockfile 存在时必须走 pnpm。
            if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
              pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
              pnpm run build
            elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
              npm ci
              npm run build
            else
              npm install
              npm run build
            fi
            cd ..

            rm -rf _afrogweb_new
            mkdir -p _afrogweb_new
            cp -r _afrogweb_tmp/build/* _afrogweb_new/
            rm -rf _afrogweb_tmp

            if [ -d "_afrogweb_new/_app/immutable/entry" ] && [ $(ls _afrogweb_new/_app/immutable/entry/*.js 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -gt 0 ]; then
              rm -rf pkg/web/webpath
              mkdir -p pkg/web/webpath
              cp -r _afrogweb_new/* pkg/web/webpath/
              WEB_ASSETS_READY=true
              echo "afrogweb assets copied successfully"
            else
              echo "afrogweb build or copy failed: no JS files in entry/" >&2
            fi
            rm -rf _afrogweb_new
          fi

          echo "WEB_ASSETS_READY=${WEB_ASSETS_READY}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

          if [ "${WEB_ASSETS_READY}" != "true" ]; then
            if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "${DRY_RUN:-}" = "true" ]; then
              echo "afrogweb assets not available (dry_run=true); continuing with placeholder assets"
            else
              echo "afrogweb assets not available. Ensure secrets.AFROGWEB_TOKEN has read access to zan8in/afrogweb." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Verify embedded web assets
        if: env.WEB_ASSETS_READY == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ls -la pkg/web/webpath || (echo "missing webpath directory" && exit 1)
          test -f pkg/web/webpath/index.html || (echo "missing index.html" && exit 1)
          test -d pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry || (echo "missing entry directory" && exit 1)
          ENTRY_COUNT=$(find pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.js' | wc -l || echo 0)
          [ "$ENTRY_COUNT" -gt 0 ] || (echo "missing entry js" && exit 1)
          CHUNKS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/chunks/*.js | wc -l)
          [ "$CHUNKS" -gt 0 ] || (echo "missing chunks js" && exit 1)

      - name: Detect unmatched web assets (embed coverage guard)
        if: env.WEB_ASSETS_READY == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          TOP_EXTS='html|ico|png|svg|webmanifest|json|txt'
          ALLOWED_TOP_RE="^pkg/web/webpath/[^/]+\.(${TOP_EXTS})$"
          ALLOWED_DIRS_RE='^pkg/web/webpath/(fonts/.+|_app/.+|docs/.+|pocs/.+|reports/.+)$'
          UNMATCHED=$(find pkg/web/webpath -type f | grep -v -E "$ALLOWED_TOP_RE" | grep -v -E "$ALLOWED_DIRS_RE" | grep -v -E "/\.DS_Store$" || true)
          if [ -n "$UNMATCHED" ]; then
            echo "[embed coverage] Detected files not covered by go:embed patterns:" >&2
            echo "$UNMATCHED" >&2
            echo "Please update pkg/web/embed.go to include these paths." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Sign official PoCs
        env:
          AFROG_POC_SIGNING_KEY_B64: ${{ secrets.AFROG_POC_SIGNING_KEY_B64 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${AFROG_POC_SIGNING_KEY_B64:-}" ]; then
            echo "AFROG_POC_SIGNING_KEY_B64 is not set; skipping official PoC signing." >&2
            echo "Embedded javascript PoCs will be unsigned (official verification disabled)." >&2
            exit 0
          fi
          go run ./cmd/afrog -pocsign pocs/afrog-pocs | tee _pocsign.out
          PUBKEY="$(sed -n 's/^pubkey=//p' _pocsign.out)"
          if [ -z "${PUBKEY}" ]; then
            echo "failed to derive the official public key from -pocsign output" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AFROG_POC_PUBKEY_B64=${PUBKEY}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

      - name: Smoke build (validate go:embed)
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: 0
        run: |
          go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o ./_afrog_smoke ./cmd/afrog
          file ./_afrog_smoke || true

      # - name: Validate embedded FS contents
      #   env:
      #     CGO_ENABLED: 0
      #   run: |
      #     set -euo pipefail

      #     # 创建临时 Go 脚本检查 embed.FS
      #     cat <<EOF > embed_check.go
      #     package main

      #     import (
      #       "embed"
      #       "fmt"
      #       "io/fs"
      #       "os"
      #       "path/filepath"
      #       "strings"
      #     )

      #     //go:embed webpath/*.*
      #     //go:embed webpath/fonts/*/*.*
      #     //go:embed webpath/_app/*.*
      #     //go:embed webpath/_app/immutable/*/*.*
      #     var webpathFS embed.FS

      #     func main() {
      #       var hasEntryJS bool
      #       err := fs.WalkDir(webpathFS, ".", func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
      #         if err != nil {
      #           return err
      #         }
      #         if !d.IsDir() && strings.HasPrefix(path, "webpath/_app/immutable/entry/") && strings.HasSuffix(path, ".js") {
      #           hasEntryJS = true
      #           fmt.Printf("Found entry JS: %s\n", path)
      #         }
      #         return nil
      #       })
      #       if err != nil {
      #         fmt.Printf("Error walking FS: %v\n", err)
      #         os.Exit(1)
      #       }
      #       if !hasEntryJS {
      #         fmt.Println("No JS files found in _app/immutable/entry/")
      #         os.Exit(1)
      #       }
      #       fmt.Println("Embedded FS validation passed")
      #     }
      #     EOF

      #     # 编译并运行检查
      #     go build -o embed_check embed_check.go
      #     ./embed_check > embed_check.log 2>&1
      #     cat embed_check.log
      #     if grep -q "validation passed" embed_check.log; then
      #       echo "Embedded FS OK"
      #     else
      #       echo "Embedded FS validation failed" >&2
      #       exit 1
      #     fi

      - name: Web smoke test (-web mode assets)
        if: env.WEB_ASSETS_READY == 'true'
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: 0
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ./_afrog_smoke -web > web_smoke.log 2>&1 & echo $! > _afrog_pid
          trap 'kill "$(cat _afrog_pid)" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          for i in $(seq 1 20); do
            if ! kill -0 "$(cat _afrog_pid)" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "web process exited early" >&2
              tail -n 200 web_smoke.log >&2 || true
              exit 1
            fi
            if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:16868/api/health | grep -q '"status":"ok"'; then
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          # 若健康检查仍未通过，输出日志并失败
          if ! curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:16868/api/health | grep -q '"status":"ok"'; then
            echo "health probe failed" >&2
            tail -n 200 web_smoke.log >&2 || true
            exit 1
          fi
          curl -fsS -I http://127.0.0.1:16868/ | grep -E "HTTP/.* 200" >/dev/null
          curl -fsS -I http://127.0.0.1:16868/ | grep -i "Content-Type: text/html" >/dev/null
          APPJS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry/*app*.js 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
          if [ -z "$APPJS" ]; then APPJS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry/*.js | head -n1 || true); fi
          APPURL=$(echo "$APPJS" | sed 's#pkg/web/webpath##')
          if [ -n "$APPURL" ]; then
            curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$APPURL" | grep -E "HTTP/.* 200" >/dev/null
            curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$APPURL" | grep -i "Content-Type: application/javascript\|Content-Type: text/javascript" >/dev/null
          fi
          STARTJS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry/*start*.js 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
          if [ -z "$STARTJS" ]; then STARTJS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/entry/*.js | head -n1 || true); fi
          STARTURL=$(echo "$STARTJS" | sed 's#pkg/web/webpath##')
          curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$STARTURL" | grep -E "HTTP/.* 200" >/dev/null
          curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$STARTURL" | grep -i "Content-Type: application/javascript\|Content-Type: text/javascript" >/dev/null
          ASSETCSS=$(ls pkg/web/webpath/_app/immutable/assets/*.css | head -n1 || true)
          if [ -n "$ASSETCSS" ]; then
            CSSURL=$(echo "$ASSETCSS" | sed 's#pkg/web/webpath##')
            curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$CSSURL" | grep -E "HTTP/.* 200" >/dev/null
            curl -fsS -I "http://127.0.0.1:16868$CSSURL" | grep -i "Content-Type: text/css" >/dev/null
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: afrog-smoke-debug
          path: |
            _afrog_smoke
            _afrog_pid
            web_smoke.log

      - name: Goreleaser snapshot (no publish)
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.dry_run == 'true'
        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v4
        with:
          args: "release --clean --snapshot --skip=publish --skip=validate"
          version: latest
          workdir: .
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"

      - name: Upload snapshot artifacts
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.dry_run == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: afrog-dist-snapshot
          path: |
            dist/**

      - name: Goreleaser publish
        if: github.event_name == 'push' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.dry_run != 'true')
        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v4
        with:
          args: "release --clean --skip=validate"
          version: latest
          workdir: .
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
",
  "rationale": "The release job has no timeout, so a hung or runaway build can consume unbounded CI minutes. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern supports bounding jobs with an explicit timeout to reduce runaway consumption, with measured savings on comparable workflows. The repository's CI history shows successful release runs completing in roughly 2-9 minutes, so a 30-minute timeout provides operational headroom without interrupting valid runs. This change adds only timeout-minutes to the existing job; it removes no steps, weakens no checks, adds no secrets, and introduces no new network access, preserving all build, verification, and release coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow. Let me analyze the evidence and the workflow.

The workflow is a "Release Binary" workflow that:
1. Triggers on push tags (v*) and workflow_dispatch
2. Has a single job "release" on ubuntu-latest
3. Steps:
   - Checkout code (fetch-depth: 0)
   - Setup Go (go-version: 1.24.1, cache: true)
   - Setup pnpm (version: 10.32.0, run_install: false)
   - Setup Node.js (node-version: 20)
   - Go modules download (go mod download)
   - Build and copy afrogweb assets (clones afrogweb repo, builds with pnpm/npm)
   - Verify embedded web assets
   - Detect unmatched web assets
   - Sign official PoCs
   - Smoke build
   - Web smoke test
   - Upload artifact (on failure)
   - Goreleaser snapshot (dry run)
   - Upload snapshot artifacts
   - Goreleaser publish

Now let me look at the evidence patterns:

1. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) - Evidence shows caching Go modules saved 6.06% elapsed time. The workflow already has `cache: true` in setup-go, but there's no explicit actions/cache for Go modules. However, setup-go's cache: true already handles Go module caching. Adding actions/cache might be redundant.

2. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (Bound jobs with custom timeout) - Evidence shows timeouts can save time. The workflow has no timeout-minutes set. Adding a timeout could be an optimization, but we need to be careful not to break valid slow runs.

3. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - Not applicable, no matrix.

4. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE - Could be applicable for release workflows on tags, but the workflow only runs on tags and dispatch. Cancel superseded runs might be relevant but the evidence says "Release or deployment work" is a contraindication. This is a release workflow, so contraindicated.

5. P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW - Contraindicated, strict contract.

6. P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER - Not really applicable for tag-based release.

Let me think about what fits best.

The workflow already uses `cache: true` in setup-go. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE evidence shows adding actions/cache for Go modules. But since setup-go already has cache: true, adding another cache might be redundant or could conflict.

Wait, looking at the experiment evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE:
- Before: setup-go@v2 without explicit cache, then go mod download
- After: added actions/cache@v4 for ~/go/pkg/mod with key based on go.mod/go.sum

In the current workflow, setup-go@v4 already has `cache: true`. So Go module caching is already done. Adding actions/cache would be redundant.

What about P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT? The workflow has no timeout. Adding a timeout-minutes could prevent runaway consumption. But we need representative successful-duration history. The CI history shows runs:
- 2026-04-29: 01:44:57 to 01:48:14 = ~3 min 17 sec
- 2026-04-28: 03:47:51 to 03:56:57 = ~9 min 6 sec
- 2026-03-12: 09:01:10 to 09:09:04 = ~7 min 54 sec
- 2026-02-27: 06:28:28 to 06:31:31 = ~3 min 3 sec
- 2026-02-27: 06:21:28 to 06:23:29 = ~2 min 1 sec

These are relatively short runs (2-9 minutes). But these are historical and might not represent all cases. The workflow does a lot: clone afrogweb, build web assets, smoke test, goreleaser. A timeout could be reasonable.

However, the instruction says "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." Adding a timeout is a minimal change that doesn't weaken coverage.

But wait - is there evidence that this specific workflow would benefit? The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT evidence shows:
- Case 1: 41s -> 30s (26.8% savings)
- Case 2: 143s -> 129s (9.8% savings)

These are measured on forks. The pattern says preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have CI history showing successful runs.

Actually, let me reconsider. The most supported optimization here might be P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, but the workflow already caches Go modules via setup-go cache: true. 

Hmm, but what about the pnpm/node dependencies? The workflow sets up pnpm and node but doesn't cache them. The setup-node@v4 doesn't have cache: true for npm. The pnpm install happens inside the "Build and copy afrogweb assets" step. There's no caching of pnpm store or node_modules.

But the evidence patterns don't specifically cover pnpm caching. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is about Go modules specifically in the example.

Let me look more carefully. The pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE says:
- Preconditions: "Repeated dependency fetching is measurable", "Cache inputs include lockfile and environment"
- Contraindications: "Mutable or untrusted cached content", "An equivalent cache already exists"

Since setup-go already has cache: true, an equivalent cache for Go modules already exists. So P-LIT-GHA-CACHE for Go modules is contraindicated.

What about P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT? 
- Preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists" - we have CI history
- Contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit"

The workflow is a release build that does web asset building, smoke testing, and goreleaser publishing. These could take variable time. Adding a timeout is risky without knowing the upper bound. But the evidence shows timeouts help.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. The instruction says "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization that fits this workflow". 

Looking at the workflow again, it has `cache: true` in setup-go. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE experiment added actions/cache for Go modules when there was no cache. Since this workflow already has it, that's not applicable.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, adding timeout-minutes to the job is a minimal, safe change that doesn't reduce coverage. The evidence supports it (measured savings). The CI history shows runs complete in under 10 minutes, so a reasonable timeout (e.g., 30 or 60 minutes) wouldn't interrupt valid runs but would prevent runaway consumption.

But wait, is there a better fit? Let me check P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE. The contraindication includes "Release or deployment work" - this IS a release workflow, so contraindicated.

P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - no matrix, not applicable.

What value? The CI history shows max ~9 minutes. A timeout of 30 minutes would give headroom. Or 60 minutes. The evidence examples used 5 minutes but those were different workflows. For this release workflow with web builds and goreleaser, 30 minutes seems reasonable.

Actually, let me reconsider whether I should use P-LIT-GHA-CACHE anyway. The workflow uses setup-go@v4 with cache: true. But the evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE specifically added actions/cache@v4. Let me go with P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. I'll add `timeout-minutes: 30` to the release job.

Wait, but I need to check: does adding a timeout weaken anything? No, it just bounds the job duration. It doesn't remove any steps or checks. It preserves all build and test coverage.

I think I should cite the pattern ID and/or experiment IDs. Let me use "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT" as the evidence ID since it's the pattern that supports this optimization.

Actually, looking at the instruction: "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." The evidence IDs would be the document_id values. Let me use the pattern document_id.

Let me construct the updated workflow. I'll add `timeout-minutes: 30` to the release job.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider if there's an even better option. 

Looking at the workflow, the "Build and copy afrogweb assets" step clones an external repo (zan8in/afrogweb.git) and builds it. This is a network access step that already exists. The optimization shouldn't add new network access.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is the cleanest fit. Let me go with that.

Let me write the updated workflow with timeout-minutes added.

Actually, I want to double-check: the evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows measured savings on forks. The pattern preconditions say "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have CI history with 5 successful runs. This satisfies the precondition.

The contraindication is "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". With a 30-minute timeout and historical runs of 2-9 minutes, this is unlikely to be an issue. But I should pick a value that gives headroom. 30 minutes is reasonable for a release build.

Let me finalize:

decision: APPLY
workflow_yaml: the updated workflow with timeout-minutes: 30 added to the release job
rationale: Adding a job timeout bounds runaway CI consumption without removing any build/test steps. Evidence from P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows custom timeouts reduce runaway consumption with measured savings. The workflow currently has no timeout, and CI history shows successful runs complete well within a 30-minute bound.
evidence_ids: ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]

Wait, I should also consider whether to cite experiment IDs. The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs". The pattern document_id is "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT". Let me include that. I could also include experiment IDs but the pattern is sufficient.

Let me write out the full YAML carefully, preserving everything exactly and just adding timeout-minutes: 30.

Actually, I realize I should think about whether 30 minutes is the right value. The evidence examples used 5 minutes, but those were for different workflows (lint, test). For a release build that builds web assets and runs goreleaser, 30 minutes is more appropriate. But I don't have strong evidence for the exact value. The pattern says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom". 30 minutes gives ~3-10x headroom over observed runs.

Let me go with 30 minutes.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider once more. Is there any issue with adding timeout-minutes to a job that has conditional steps and goreleaser? No, timeout-minutes just cancels the job if it exceeds the limit. It doesn't interfere with step conditionals.

OK, I'm confident. Let me write the response.

One more thing - I need to make sure the YAML is valid and complete. Let me copy the original and add `timeout-minutes: 30` after `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`.

```yaml

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
```

Updated:
```yaml
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

```

That's the only change. Minimal and preserves everything.
